title: Let him go up (2 Chronicles 36:23)
hookLine: the Hebrew Bible ends with Cyrus's call to go up and rebuild

cards: The second-to-last scene is a ruin. At the end of Second Chronicles, the Babylonians burn the house of God, break down the wall of Jerusalem, and carry the survivors away to Babylon.
The land lay desolate and kept its sabbaths, the text says, as the word of the LORD by Jeremiah had said. If the book stopped there, the whole Hebrew Bible would close on smoke and exile.
A new king, Cyrus of Persia, sends a proclamation through all his kingdom, in speech and in writing. And in the order this path follows, the last word of the whole Tanakh is a verb of movement.

teach.b: Here is the final verse, in the King James words: "Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath the LORD God of heaven given me; and he hath charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who is there among you of all his people? The LORD his God be with him, and let him go up."
And there it stops. In Hebrew, the very last word is ve-ya'al: and let him go up.
Eight days ago we heard this same decree open the book of Ezra, and there the sentence keeps going: let him go up to Jerusalem, and build the house of the LORD.
Chronicles stops one breath sooner. No Jerusalem yet, no building, no arrival. Just a question, a blessing, and the first step of a road.
Some readers hear in it the word aliyah, a going up: being called up to the Torah in synagogue is an aliyah, and so is moving to the land of Israel. Now look back at this week.
Ezra set his heart. Nehemiah's slow work was done before. The builders kept one hand on the stone.
The Levites gave the sense. Joy became strength. Chronicles reached from Adam to now.
And the whole library closes on let him go up: not with the building done, but with the call to keep climbing.

how: In synagogue, being called up to say the blessings over the Torah reading is called an aliyah, a going up, and moving to the land of Israel is also called making aliyah.

o: and let him go up: the Hebrew Bible's last word
and they wept: the exiles mourning in Babylon
and he built: the Temple finished at the end

games.q: this week, day by day — tap the pairs.

s: the Hebrew Bible ends with the Temple in ruins
it ends two verses later, with Cyrus's call to go up and rebuild.
the last word of the Tanakh means and let him go up
ve-ya'al, the last word of 2 Chronicles 36:23.
Cyrus's proclamation appears only once in the Bible
it appears again at the start of the book of Ezra.

games.q: you're compiling the last page of a long library. the story has just reached the destruction of Jerusalem. how do you end?
o: on a call to go up and rebuild.
with a summary of everything before.
games.why: the Hebrew Bible closes on Cyrus: "the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up."

practice: Sit tall and hear Cyrus's question as if it were asked of you: who is there among you? Think of one place you've been stuck in the ruins a while, something left broken or put off, and choose one step up, small enough to take.
If you pray, ask in words from your tradition for help to go up.

wordCard.voice: Ve-ya'al. And let him go up: the last words of the Hebrew Bible, Cyrus's call to the people, and let them go up and rebuild. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: and let him go up, the last word of 2 Chronicles 36:23. in Ezra 1:3 the same word is followed by 'to Jerusalem'.

carryVoice: Your line: the call to keep climbing. The road starts before the destination is on the page. That's day eight hundred eighty-two.
